text: Each call that fails with `SqlWorkersBusyError` produces exactly one rejection `WARNING` record (distinct from the saturation warning) on the `sqllens.agent.integrations.sql_threads` logger, including rejections that occur within `SATURATION_WARNING_INTERVAL_S` of a saturation warning; a unit test that times out several queued calls in one burst sees one rejection record per rejected call. No rejection record contains the call's SQL, arguments or exception message.

On Python 3.11 and 3.12, a unit test that grants a waiting call its slot and cancels that call in the same loop tick sees the caller raise `CancelledError`, the call never run, and the slot still available to a later call.

The `sql_threads.py` module docstring and `docs/internal/mcp-server/transport.md` state that the slot limit, the wait limit and the saturation warning assume all SQL calls run on one event loop at a time, and that calls from a second concurrently running loop get their own slots and may wait in the shared executor's queue, where neither the wait limit nor the warning applies.

When the release of a slot fails because its event loop is closed, no `ERROR` record is written on the `sqllens.agent.integrations.sql_threads` logger and nothing propagates; when scheduling the release raises a `RuntimeError` while the loop is still open, one `ERROR` record naming the exception type is written on that logger and nothing propagates. Unit tests cover both cases.
A unit test makes `submit` raise and then shows that `SQL_WORKER_THREADS` calls on that loop all start without waiting for a slot.
Every SQL worker pool test in `tests/unit/test_sql_runner_event_loop.py` runs on an executor no earlier test used.
Every test under `tests/integration/` starts with `sqllens.tools._agent._AGENT_STATE` set to `None`, as every unit test already does.
The `run_sql` docstrings of the SQLite, MySQL and Postgres runners list `SqlWorkersBusyError` under `Raises:`.

An integration test holds two `query_database` runs, from two different conversations, open at the local model stand-in at the same time; while both are held, `/healthz` and `list_data_sources` on another session each answer within 2 s, and once released both runs return a result that is not an error.

The change leaves the slot semaphore keyed per event loop and the worker executor process-wide, adds no file under `changelog.d/`, and leaves `changelog.d/300.fixed.md` unchanged, including its sentence that a query waiting more than a minute for a free worker fails with "All database workers are busy; try again shortly."
